seoDescription: Learn the fundamentals of templating in October CMS by building a basic website structure from scratch. This tutorial guides you through creating and integrating reusable partials for your header and footer, organizing your layout with CSS classes, and constructing a dynamic navigation menu. Discover how to use October's Twig-based templating language to generate page links and apply active class states for a better user experience. Master these essential skills to efficiently structure your October CMS projects.

chapters.title: Introduction to Basic Templating
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the goal of organizing the page layout using HTML, pre-written CSS, and the October CMS templating language.

chapters.title: Creating and Including a Header Partial
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to create a header partial and include it in the main layout file using the Twig partial tag.

chapters.title: Using the Twig Partial Tag
chapters.description: This part explains how to use the Twig `partial` tag to render a partial file, noting that the folder and extension are automatically inferred by October CMS.

chapters.title: Building the Header Markup
chapters.description: This chapter covers writing the HTML structure for the site header within the newly created partial file, including a logo and container.

chapters.title: Creating and Including the Footer Partial
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to create a footer partial, add content to it, and include it in the default layout just like the header.

chapters.title: Adding Content to the Homepage
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to add placeholder content directly into the homepage page file to populate the main content area.

chapters.title: Building a Navigation Menu with Twig Links
chapters.description: This part walks through creating a navigation menu in the header partial and using the Twig `page` filter to dynamically generate links.

chapters.title: Linking to Other Pages and Fixing Layouts
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to add a link for the movies page and then corrects its appearance by applying the default layout to the page file.

chapters.title: Implementing Active Menu States with Twig
chapters.description: This chapter details how to dynamically add an 'active' class to the current menu item using a Twig conditional and the `this.page.id` variable.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Next Steps
chapters.description: This final chapter summarizes the basic templating concepts covered and gives a brief preview of what is to come in the series.

summary:
## Key Concepts: Basic Theming in October CMS This document outlines the fundamental techniques for structuring a website's theme using October CMS's templating language. ### Layouts and Partials The foundation of theming in October CMS involves separating your code into layouts, pages, and partials. - **Layouts (`default.htm`):** Define the main HTML structure (``, ``, ``) that's shared across multiple pages. They act as a shell where page-specific content is injected. - **Partials (`header.htm`, `footer.htm`):** Contain reusable chunks of HTML, like headers, footers, or sidebars. This avoids code duplication and makes maintenance easier. > [!TIP] > To include a partial in a layout or page, use the Twig tag `{% partial 'partial-name' %}`. You don't need to specify the `.htm` extension or the `/partials/` directory path. ### Dynamic Page Linking with Twig Hard-coding URLs is fragile. October CMS provides a robust way to link between pages using the **`| page` filter**. - **Usage:** Create links by passing the page's ID (its filename without the extension) to the filter. - **Example:** `Movies` will generate the correct URL for the `movies.htm` page. > [!IMPORTANT] > This approach ensures that your links will not break even if the URL structure of your site changes. ### Creating an Active Navigation State To provide visual feedback to users, you can highlight the current page in the navigation menu. This is achieved with a simple Twig conditional. - **Key Variable:** The `this.page.id` variable contains the ID of the currently rendered page. - **Implementation:** Use a ternary operator within the `class` attribute of your list item. **Example Code:** ```twig
  • Home
  • Movies
    • ``` This code checks if the current page's ID matches 'homepage' or 'movies' and adds the `active` class accordingly. The corresponding CSS will then style the active menu item differently. ### Assigning Layouts to Pages If a page appears unstyled, it may not have a layout assigned. You can fix this by adding the `layout` property to the configuration section at the top of the page's `.htm` file. **Example in `movies.htm`:** ```ini url = "/movies" layout = "default" title = "Movies" ==

    This is the movies page.

    ```
